sources.title: Repository source identifying Rotate List / LeetCode 61 and boundary audit
Deterministic JDK 21 exact-fence rotate-list structural validation

claims.text: The repository source identifies Rotate List as LeetCode 61 but does not locally preserve the full platform statement, ListNode declaration, bounds or negative-k semantics.
Under the explicitly stated right-rotation/non-negative-k contract, the exact candidate relinks the original nodes via length/modulo/ring/cut in O(n) time and O(1) auxiliary space.
The executable fixture verifies value order, original node identities, no lost/duplicate nodes and no residual cycle across boundary cases.
Independent review found no hard failures or uncovered source variants and validated exact node identity order/no-cycle invariants over bounded exhaustive n/k cases.

findings: The preserved source identifies Rotate List as LeetCode 61 and coding intent, but the local source does not preserve the full platform statement, ListNode declaration, bounds, or negative-k semantics.
The candidate explicitly states a narrow right-rotation/non-negative-k contract and marks negative-k rejection as answer-side policy rather than recovered source.
The length/modulo/temporary-ring/cut algorithm preserves the original nodes, runs in O(n) time with O(1) auxiliary space, and explains the cut position rather than only presenting code.
The exact Java fence independently passed an identity-based oracle for every n<=8 and k<=40 plus huge k, proving expected node order, no lost/duplicated nodes and no residual cycle.
The answer calls out empty/singleton/modulo boundaries and does not fabricate project experience.
